sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Today, 20 September 2026, the OpenAI robotics salary story is a careers-board count, not a product drop. [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/openai-is-offering-robotics-engineers-up-to-500-000-in-salary-2026-9) reviewed the public listings on 18 September and counted 27 robotics jobs, up from 11 in May. Advertised base pay runs from $177,000 to $500,000 before equity. [The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/openai-robotics-engineer-salaries-500000) counted 21 San Francisco robotics roles the same day. Cite the reviewer for the headcount. Do not invent a single official total.

The $500,000 ceiling is a named ID. OpenAI's [Machine Learning Engineer, Distributed Data Systems - Robotics](https://openai.com/careers/machine-learning-engineer-distributed-data-systems-robotics-san-francisco/) listing pays $380,000 to $500,000 plus equity. The work is distributed compute, orchestration, storage, streaming, and multimodal training pipelines. [Ashby](https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/openai/4a13c764-18c3-4076-ac87-29e05491be07) dated that posting 6 February 2026. Sunday is not a new pay scale. It is a larger board sitting on a band that has been public for months.

This is not a [GPT-6 Astra](/blog/gpt-6-astra-computer-use-flagship) computer-use remap, and it is not the [OpenAI Agents API](/blog/openai-agents-api-codex-harness). Those are software SKUs. The robotics listings describe workcells, data-collection labs, and on-site San Francisco days. [Sam Altman](https://x.com/sama/status/2061117302528188712) said on 31 May that OpenAI Robotics is hiring hardware, ops, systems, and ML engineers for robots that help skilled workers build infrastructure, with a personal robot as the long-term picture. A hiring post is not a ship date.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Searchers asking what the OpenAI robotics salary is have a verified split. The top dollar is a data job. [The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/openai-robotics-engineer-salaries-500000) put that in the headline: the $500,000 role does not pay people to build robots on the bench. An [Inference Engineer, Robotics](https://openai.com/careers/inference-engineer-robotics-san-francisco/) listing is a flat $380,000 plus equity for GPU serving and inference-friendly model design. A [Robotics Software Engineer](https://openai.com/careers/robotics-software-engineer-san-francisco/) who needs five years and Rust or C++ is $255,000 to $325,000. Control systems sit at $380,000 to $460,000. Field engineering is $266,000 to $380,000 to keep data-acquisition workcells up.

The 2021 shutdown is the other split. [VentureBeat](https://venturebeat.com/business/openai-disbands-its-robotics-research-team) recorded Wojciech Zaremba saying the first robotics team stopped because data, not the approach, was missing. The current IDs read like a fix for that failure: data systems at the top of the band, software to grow collection labs, field engineers on the floor. [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/327751/20260920/openai-posts-500k-robotics-salaries-fund-data-factory-behind-its-robot-comeback.htm) calls the San Francisco site a three-shift teleoperation lab on GELLO controllers and Franka arms, grown from about 100 contractors to more than 400. That shop-floor picture is a recap. It is not on the careers pages. Score the listings. Treat the shift count as reported color.

The job question is narrower than the [2030 economy-wide scenarios](/blog/anthropic-ai-jobs-2030-econ-scenarios) and different from [Anthropic's R&D Automation Index](/blog/anthropic-rd-automation-index-claude). Those meters track Claude leading lab work. This board tracks humans OpenAI will pay to manufacture robot demonstrations. It is also not [Meta's Project OT cuts](/blog/meta-project-ot-ai-job-cuts). Sunday is a hire signal. It is not a layoff memo, and it is not proof that a personal robot is on a price list.

paragraphs: Robotics and physical-AI engineers feel it first. Figure, Physical Intelligence, Tesla Optimus, 1X, and Apptronik already bid for the same small pool. OpenAI's public base for data-systems ML sits at the top of that pile before equity. Hardware IDs for actuator design, firmware, PCB layout, and prototyping often have no published range in the recaps. Do not treat a missing number as a cheap seat. Treat it as an unpriced negotiation.

Cloud, facilities, and capital desks sit one layer out. The [San Francisco Chronicle](https://www.sfchronicle.com/tech/article/openai-richmond-warehouse-robotics-22160624.php) dated the Richmond lease in March: 202,000 square feet at 1411 Harbour Way S., about 15.75 acres, more than 14,000 amps, formerly planned for Moxion Power. The [Business Times](https://www.bizjournals.com/sanfrancisco/news/2026/04/16/openai-richmond-east-bay-lease.html) later said the term is at least ten years with extension options and a right of first offer to buy. That is industrial power and time. It is not a SKU. Pair it with the [SoftBank loan](/blog/softbank-openai-11-9-billion-loan) only as a funding backdrop. Do not paste a warehouse amp rating onto a [Jalapeño inference chip](/blog/openai-jalapeno-inference-chip) roadmap.

Policy and talent teams sit one layer up. Altman's May note named infrastructure build-out first and a personal robot later. Caitlin Kalinowski, hired from Meta in late 2024 to lead hardware and robotics, resigned in March. The Next Web says no replacement is named on the listings. A board without a public lead is a hiring fact. It is not a product cancel. Compare the desks to [roles being created](/blog/ai-jobs-roles-at-risk-and-roles-being-created), not to [ChatGPT for Financial Services](/blog/chatgpt-for-financial-services-junior-bankers). Junior banker work is a software seat. This board is a floor and a pipeline.

sections.heading: Facts versus predictions
paragraphs: Fact: OpenAI lists a Machine Learning Engineer, Distributed Data Systems - Robotics role in San Francisco at $380,000 to $500,000 base plus equity. Fact: related public bands include Inference Engineer at $380,000, Control Systems Software Engineer at $380,000 to $460,000, Robotics Software Engineer at $255,000 to $325,000, and Field Engineer at $266,000 to $380,000. Fact: Business Insider counted 27 robotics-related listings on 18 September 2026, up from 11 in May, with advertised bases from $177,000 to $500,000. Fact: The Next Web counted 21 the same day. Fact: Ashby dated the $500,000 ML posting 6 February 2026. Fact: OpenAI leased about 202,000 square feet at 1411 Harbour Way S. in Richmond in March 2026. Fact: this is not a consumer robot launch and not a 2026 IPO event.

Prediction: most applicants will chase the $500,000 headline and miss that the ID is a data-platform job posted in February. Prediction: humanoid startups will feel the bid more on pipeline and inference talent than on PCB layout, because those bands are public. Prediction: headlines will call Sunday a robot comeback. The listings are a data factory and a warehouse. Do not treat 27 open reqs as a ship date, and do not treat $500,000 as the typical OpenAI robotics salary.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch whether OpenAI publishes a single robotics careers index, or whether 21 and 27 keep drifting by how reviewers tag adjacent IDs. Watch whether the $500,000 ML role fills, closes, or stays evergreen. Watch whether Richmond job text moves from San Francisco-first to an East Bay reporting line. Watch whether a named hardware lead replaces Kalinowski. Watch first-party confirmation of the three-shift teleoperation story. And watch the [IPO delay](/blog/openai-ipo-delay-2026-safety) against this hire wave. A data factory can grow while a listing waits. A consumer robot still needs a model card, a safety case, and a price.

sections.heading: FAQ
paragraphs: What is the OpenAI robotics salary? The highest public robotics base on OpenAI's careers pages is $380,000 to $500,000 plus equity for Machine Learning Engineer, Distributed Data Systems - Robotics. Other listed bases include $380,000 for Inference Engineer, $380,000 to $460,000 for Control Systems Software Engineer, $255,000 to $325,000 for Robotics Software Engineer, and $266,000 to $380,000 for Field Engineer. Business Insider's 18 September review put the advertised robotics range at $177,000 to $500,000 before equity.

Is OpenAI hiring robotics engineers? Yes. Business Insider counted 27 robotics-related listings on 18 September 2026, up from 11 in May. The Next Web counted 21 San Francisco robotics jobs the same day. Sam Altman posted a hiring call for OpenAI Robotics on 31 May 2026. Check the live careers IDs. Recaps disagree on the exact total.

Does the $500,000 OpenAI robotics salary pay people who build robots? Not as the primary job. The $500,000 ceiling is the distributed-data ML listing: pipelines, storage, streaming, and multimodal training infrastructure. Hardware roles such as actuator design, firmware, and PCB layout often have no public base in the recaps. Software and field roles that keep data-collection cells running sit below the $500,000 cap.

What is OpenAI building in Richmond? County-cited reporting says OpenAI leased about 202,000 square feet at 1411 Harbour Way S. in Richmond in March 2026, on a waterfront site with more than 14,000 amps. The Business Times later described a lease of at least ten years with extension options. That is industrial space and power for robotics operations. It is not a named consumer product.

Is OpenAI shipping a consumer robot? No public SKU, price, or generally available robot is attached to this week's careers-board story. Altman's May note framed near-term work as robots that support skilled workers on infrastructure, and a personal robot as a long-term picture. Score open jobs and a warehouse lease. Do not score a humanoid you can order.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Today, 20 September 2026, StepFun put a name on a model that Artificial Analysis had already been scoring. [Step 5 Preview](https://www.stepfun.com/step-5-preview) is the company's new flagship for agentic work. The documented model ID is `step-5-preview`. The [platform guide](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/guides/models/step-5-preview) lists a 1 million token input window, a 64,000 token maximum output, native text, image, and video in, and text out. StepFun's product page adds the architecture: a 600 billion parameter sparse mixture of experts with 27 billion parameters active per token. API and Studio access opened the same day.

This is not [Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock](/blog/kimi-k3-amazon-bedrock). K3 already has July open weights and an 18 September hosted SKU. Sunday is a StepFun ID on StepFun's meter. It is also not a self-host. StepFun says open weights follow on 15 October. [OrcaRouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai/blog/step-5-preview-open-weights) dated the Hugging Face namespace `stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview-BF16` to 20 September at 03:52 UTC and found a single `.gitattributes` file: no shards, no license, no model card. Score a callable preview. Do not score a checkpoint you can load tonight.

Two meters matter, and they are not the same clock as a weights drop. [Pricing docs](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/guides/pricing/details) list cache-miss input at $1.00 per million tokens, cache-hit input at $0.05, and output at $2.70. Cache-miss input includes writing new content to the cache. Output tokens include reasoning and the final answer. [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/step-5) scores the reasoning SKU at 44 on Intelligence Index v4.3.2, with $1.00 in, $2.70 out, a 95 percent cache discount, 99.8 output tokens per second, and 2.96 seconds to first token. The board dates the model 18 September, two days before the announcement. Cite Sunday for availability. Cite the independent table for the bill.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Searchers asking whether Step 5 Preview is available now have a verified split. The API is on. The weights are a calendar date. [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/stepfun-ships-step-5-preview-api-a-600b-moe-at-1270-that-scores-44-on) put the same split in one line: callable today, downloadable on 15 October. A team that needs a bake-off ID can start. A team that needs a license file, a config, and a cluster recipe cannot. [NVIDIA's Hugging Face deal](/blog/nvidia-buys-hugging-face-open-model-hub) did not fill that repo. A reserved BF16 name is a scheduling signal. It is not a weight.

The independent table is the other split. Artificial Analysis places Step 5 Preview at 44, matching the Kimi K3 class on the same index, at roughly a third of Bedrock Global's $3/$15 list and far below Claude Opus 5's $5/$25. Cost per Intelligence Index task is $0.71. The run burned 160 million output tokens against a 92 million median, and $922.84 to complete the index. Verbosity eats some of the sticker. [DeepSeek V4.1 Flash](/blog/deepseek-v4-1-flash-pricing-api-benchmarks) is still cheaper per token at $0.15/$0.60. Flash is not a 44. The [broader pricing reset](/blog/ai-model-pricing-is-changing-what-teams-can-ship) still applies: dollars per resolved task after reasoning tokens, not dollars per pretty million.

The window is not unlimited in both directions. StepFun documents 1 million tokens of input and 64,000 tokens of output. OrcaRouter had flagged a 350,000 / 64,000 pair in circulating tooling. The output cap is now first-party. Long-horizon agents that dump traces into the completion will hit 64k before they hit 1M. Sparse activation is also not a laptop story. 27 billion active parameters per token is about 4.5 percent of 600 billion. The inactive experts still have to live in memory. [Data Studios](https://www.datastudios.org/post/stepfun-launches-step-5-preview-with-600b-parameters-1m-context-and-open-weights-coming-october-15) put BF16 at about 1.2 TB before runtime overhead. Score a hosted 600B. Do not staff a 27B box.

sections.heading: Who is affected

image.alt: Diagram comparing Step 5 Preview on StepFun's API as of 20 September 2026, the 15 October open-weights date, and Kimi K3 which already has July weights plus an 18 September Amazon Bedrock SKU
image.caption: An API ID is a meter. A weights date is a promise. Kimi K3 already ships both. Do not collapse the three.

paragraphs: Agent and coding teams feel it first. Point long-context software work, document research, and finance write-ups at `step-5-preview`, with `reasoning_effort` set to low, medium, or high on Chat Completions, or `output_config.effort` on the Messages API. The guide allows up to 60 images, video as URL, Base64, or `stepfile://`, and MP4 files under 128 MB. Tool calling, JSON Mode, JSON Schema, streaming, and prompt caching are on. Tools still belong to the app. The model does not reach your laptop or the open web by itself. Do not paste a [GPT-6 Astra](/blog/gpt-6-astra-computer-use-flagship) computer-use graph onto a StepFun WebSocket and call it a cutover.

Platform and procurement teams sit one layer out. Artificial Analysis lists a single provider: StepFun. There is no Bedrock row, no OpenRouter row, and no second region in the independent table. [RuntimeWire](https://runtimewire.com/article/stepfun-step-5-preview-600b-agent-model-pricing) notes public rate limits, geographic restrictions, and enterprise terms are still thin outside the published top-up ladder. A V0 account is 5 concurrent requests, 10 RPM, and 5 million TPM. That is a trial, not a contact-center fleet. The [Step Plan](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/step-plan/overview) overview still names `step-3.7-flash` as the subscription flagship. The Step 5 Preview page points Claude Code users at Step Plan for 1M context. Treat that as a watch item, not as proof the ID is inside every monthly SKU.

Self-host and eval teams sit one layer up. Until 15 October, the only billable path is StepFun's API. Vendor-published rows on DeepSWE v1.1 (67.7), StepCodeBench (49.0), Terminal-Bench v4 (33.3), FrontierFinance (66.4), and DRACO (83.3) are StepFun's table. Artificial Analysis independently records 33.3 percent on Terminal-Bench 4.0. The 1/8 Claude Opus 5 task-cost claim is also StepFun's, without a public task mix. Bake the preview against Kimi K3 and your own traces. Do not take a house benchmark as a migration warrant, and do not treat a 44 as proof you can skip evals.

sections.heading: Facts versus predictions
paragraphs: Fact: StepFun announced Step 5 Preview on 20 September 2026 and opened API and Studio access the same day under the ID `step-5-preview`. Fact: the platform guide lists a 1 million token input window, a 64,000 token maximum output, and text, image, and video input with text output. Fact: StepFun describes a 600B sparse MoE with 27B parameters active per token. Fact: paid API pricing is $1.00 per million cache-miss input tokens, $0.05 per million cache-hit input tokens, and $2.70 per million output tokens, with output including reasoning. Fact: Artificial Analysis scores Step 5 Preview at 44 on the Intelligence Index, $0.71 per index task, 99.8 tokens per second, 2.96 seconds to first token, and lists StepFun as the only provider. Fact: StepFun says open weights ship on 15 October 2026. Fact: this is not Kimi K3, and it is not a downloadable checkpoint today.

Prediction: most broken 3.7 Flash graphs will land on `step-5-preview` for the 1M window, not because 33.3 percent Terminal-Bench beats GPT-6 Astra's vendor-reported 57.9, but because the meter is $1/$2.70. Prediction: cache hit rate and reasoning tokens, not GPQA, will decide whether the ID stays in a production router next to [Kimi K3](/blog/kimi-k3-amazon-bedrock). Prediction: headlines will call Sunday an open-weight launch. The repo is a name. 15 October is the test. Do not treat a 44 as a frontier crown, and do not treat $1.00 as a flat million-token tax.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch whether `stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview-BF16` fills on 15 October, and with what license. Watch whether a config file confirms 600B total and 27B active. Watch whether Step Plan adds a dedicated `step-5-preview` row, or keeps pointing Claude Code at 3.7 Flash. Watch independent Terminal-Bench and finance reruns against StepFun's house table. Watch whether the 64k output cap is enough for agent traces, or whether teams start summarizing the model's own reasoning to stay under it. Watch second providers. A one-vendor 44 is a bake-off ID, not a multi-cloud SKU. And watch the weights versus API question. If a workload has to run on Sunday, it needs `step-5-preview` and a measured cache window, not a rumor that the BF16 repo is already a cluster.

sections.heading: FAQ
paragraphs: What is Step 5 Preview? It is StepFun's flagship agentic model, announced 20 September 2026 under the ID `step-5-preview`. StepFun describes a 600 billion parameter sparse mixture of experts with 27 billion parameters active per token. The platform guide lists a 1 million token input window, a 64,000 token maximum output, and text, image, and video input with text output. It is a hosted preview. It is not an open-weight checkpoint today.

Is Step 5 Preview available? Yes, on StepFun's API and Studio as of 20 September 2026. Artificial Analysis lists StepFun as the only provider. Open weights are scheduled for 15 October. Recaps of the Hugging Face namespace `stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview-BF16` still describe a placeholder, not shards. Step Plan's public model list still leads with `step-3.7-flash`. Check the ID before you assume the monthly SKU includes it.

How much does Step 5 Preview cost? On the paid StepFun API, cache-miss input is $1.00 per million tokens, cache-hit input is $0.05, and output is $2.70. Output includes reasoning tokens. Artificial Analysis reports a 95 percent cache discount, $0.71 per Intelligence Index task, and a 7:2:1 blended rate of $0.51 per million tokens. Rate limits follow the account top-up ladder, starting at 10 RPM on a V0 account.

When will Step 5 Preview open weights ship? StepFun's product page says 15 October 2026. Until that date, treat the model as proprietary API access. The reserved BF16 repository is a scheduling claim. It is not evidence that self-hosting is possible this week. License, quantization, and cluster recipes are unknown until the files exist.

Is Step 5 Preview the same as Kimi K3? No. Kimi K3 is Moonshot's 2.8T open-weight flagship, with July Hugging Face weights and an 18 September Amazon Bedrock SKU at $3/$15 Global. Step 5 Preview is StepFun's 600B hosted preview at $1/$2.70. Artificial Analysis scores both at 44 on the Intelligence Index. Bake them off. Do not remap them.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Today, 20 September 2026, buyers are still mapping Tuesday's Live API drop. [Gemini 3.8 Live](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-3-8-live-gemini-3-8-live-extended-thinking/) and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking listed as generally available on 15 September. The named products are `gemini-3.8-live` and `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking`. Google's developer note prices both at $0.005 per minute of audio input and $0.018 per minute of audio output, the same $3/$12 per million audio-token row as `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`. [9to5Google](https://9to5google.com/2026/09/15/gemini-3-8-live-announced/) dated the consumer recap the same day: Search Live for the base SKU, Gemini Live plus Docs, Gmail, and Keep for Extended Thinking.

This is not [Gemini 3.8 Flash](/blog/gemini-3-8-flash-agent-workhorse). Flash is the 1 million token text workhorse at $0.75/$3.75. Gemini 3.8 Live is a native speech-to-speech pair based on Gemini 3 Pro. The [model card](https://deepmind.google/models/model-cards/gemini-3-8-audio) lists a 128K input window, 64K output, image and video in, audio and text out, and a January 2025 knowledge cutoff. API docs publish 131,072 / 65,536. Caching, code execution, file search, and structured outputs are off. The Live API itself remains in preview.

Two meters matter, and they are not the same clock as [GPT-Live-1](/blog/gpt-live-1-voice-api-pricing). Google's list is token-based, with a per-minute estimate of about 25 audio tokens per second. [Live API billing docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/best-practices) say every turn re-bills the accumulated native-audio context. Proactive audio is permanently on for both 3.8 Live SKUs, so input tokens accrue while the session is listening. Video frames are sent by default. Score a hosted voice ID with a compounding window. Do not score a Flash remap, and do not score OpenAI's $0.05 occupied-minute layer.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Searchers asking whether Gemini 3.8 Live is available now have a verified split. Tuesday is a Live API GA, plus Search Live and Gemini Live surfaces. It is not a silent Flash point release. The predecessor to migrate is `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`. Google's migration notes drop `thinking_level` on the base SKU, lock proactive audio on, and default turn coverage to audio activity plus all video. Affective dialogue is gone. Audio is the supported response modality. Turn on output transcription if you need a text log, and budget that as extra text-output tokens.

The independent table is the other split. [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/speech-to-speech) ranks Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) first on the Speech to Speech Index at 82.6, with 68.6% on τ-Voice, 98% speech reasoning, 1.35 seconds to first audio, and $3.50 per hour of input audio on its Big Bench subset. The base Gemini 3.8 Live SKU sits at 76.0, with 30.1% agentic, 96.1% conversational dynamics, 1083 Arena Elo, 1.18 seconds to first audio, and $0.84 per input hour. Google also cites 35.1% on Sierra's τ-Voice-banking set and 97.7% on Big Bench Audio for Extended Thinking. Preference and agentic skill have decoupled. The cheap SKU is the one people prefer talking to. The thinking SKU is the one that finishes tool-heavy calls.

The sticker is not the bill. GPT-Live-1 is $0.05 per occupied minute plus a backend model. Gemini 3.8 Live's headline $0.005/$0.018 only holds if you compress the window. Without `contextWindowCompression`, Google says audio-only sessions hit about 15 minutes and audio-video sessions about 2 minutes before the native-audio pile-up. That is the Live half of [how model pricing changes what teams can ship](/blog/ai-model-pricing-is-changing-what-teams-can-ship): dollars per resolved call after re-billing, not dollars per pretty minute.

paragraphs: Voice-agent and contact-center teams feel it first. Point high-volume triage, language practice, and fast tools at `gemini-3.8-live`. Point multi-step bookings, diagnostics, and long tool latency at `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking`, with `thinking_level` set to low, medium, or high. MINIMAL returns an error. Extended Thinking requires `behavior: NON_BLOCKING` on every function. `turnComplete: true` only ends an utterance. The session is idle when `interaction_status` is `IDLE`. Do not paste a Flash agent graph onto a Live WebSocket and call it a cutover.

Platform teams sit one layer out. Google named Agora, Fishjam, LiveKit, LangChain, Pipecat, Vercel, and Vision Agents as Live API integration partners. Salesforce is on the customer list next to [Agentforce job-ready agents](/blog/salesforce-agentforce-job-ready-agents). That is a telephony and CX path. It is not the [OpenAI Agents API](/blog/openai-agents-api-codex-harness). All generated audio carries a SynthID watermark. The model card still lists Vertex AI among distribution channels, but Tuesday's developer GA is Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Enterprise is a private preview in Gemini Enterprise.

Procurement and Workspace admins sit one layer up. Google AI Pro and Ultra get Extended Thinking in Docs Live. All Google AI subscribers get it in Gmail Live and Keep Live. Search Live uses the base SKU. [Siri's private delegation hooks](/blog/siri-model-delegation-claude-chatgpt) are a different assistant bet: Apple still holds the switch. Gemini 3.8 Live is already on. Treat Vertex GA, session-resumption token lifetime (two hours after last close), and GoAway handling as watch items, not findings. A Chinese-language or 97-language claim in the blog is also a watch item. Live API overview copy still lags on language count.

sections.heading: Facts versus predictions
paragraphs: Fact: Google announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking on 15 September 2026, with model IDs `gemini-3.8-live` and `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking`. Fact: developer audio pricing is $3.00 per million input tokens or $0.005 per minute, and $12.00 per million output tokens or $0.018 per minute; text is $0.75 in and $4.50 out, including thinking tokens; image and video input is $1.00 per million or $0.002 per minute. Fact: Artificial Analysis lists Extended Thinking (High) at 82.6 on the Speech to Speech Index and 68.6% on τ-Voice, and lists Gemini 3.8 Live at 76.0, 1083 Arena Elo, and $0.84 per input hour. Fact: caching is unsupported, proactive audio is permanently enabled, and the Live API remains in preview. Fact: the knowledge cutoff is January 2025. Fact: this is not Gemini 3.8 Flash.

Prediction: most broken 3.1 Flash Live graphs will land on `gemini-3.8-live`, not Extended Thinking, because 30.1% τ-Voice still beats a 1.35 second thinking pause for simple IVR. Prediction: compounding audio re-billing, not GPQA, will decide whether Gemini 3.8 Live stays in a production router next to [GPT-Live-1](/blog/gpt-live-1-voice-api-pricing). Prediction: headlines will call Tuesday a Gemini 3.8 launch. The text workhorse already shipped. Tuesday is distribution for speech. Do not treat an 82.6 index as proof you can skip evals, and do not treat $0.005 as a flat minute tax.

paragraphs: Watch whether Google adds a dedicated pricing row for the 3.8 Live IDs, or whether they keep sharing the 3.1 Flash Live Preview card. Watch context-window compression hit rates once 15-minute calls are in production. Watch Vertex GA versus the private Gemini Enterprise preview. Watch independent τ-Voice-banking reruns against the 35.1% Sierra clip. Watch whether video-by-default stays a cost trap or gets an off switch that does not break visual grounding. Watch SynthID detection in the contact-center recording stack. And watch the Flash versus Live question. If a workload has to speak on Tuesday, it needs a Live model ID and a measured compression window, not a rumor that 3.8 Flash now does voice.

sections.heading: FAQ
paragraphs: What is Gemini 3.8 Live? It is Google DeepMind's native audio-to-audio Live API model, generally available as of 15 September 2026 under the ID `gemini-3.8-live`. It takes text, images, audio, and video, and it outputs audio and text. The sibling SKU is Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking. Both are based on Gemini 3 Pro. They are not Gemini 3.8 Flash.

Is Gemini 3.8 Live available? Yes. Google lists developer access in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, Search Live for the base SKU, and Gemini Live plus Workspace Docs, Gmail, and Keep for Extended Thinking. Gemini Enterprise is a private preview. The Live API itself is still documented as preview. The predecessor to migrate is `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`.

How much does Gemini 3.8 Live cost? On the paid Gemini API, audio is $3.00 per million input tokens or about $0.005 per minute, and $12.00 per million output tokens or about $0.018 per minute. Text is $0.75 input and $4.50 output per million tokens, including thinking. Image and video input is $1.00 per million tokens or $0.002 per minute. The Live API re-bills accumulated native-audio context every turn. Compression is required for long sessions.

What is Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking? It is the high-reasoning Live SKU, `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking`. It plans and calls asynchronous tools in the background while speaking fillers. thinking_level is low, medium, or high. MINIMAL is not supported. Tools must be NON_BLOCKING. Artificial Analysis ranks the High setting first on the Speech to Speech Index at 82.6, with 68.6% on τ-Voice.

Is Gemini 3.8 Live the same as Gemini 3.8 Flash or GPT-Live-1? No. Flash is the cheap text agent workhorse with a 1 million token window. GPT-Live-1 is OpenAI's $0.05 per minute voice layer with a separate backend model. Gemini 3.8 Live is a native speech-to-speech pair with a 128K-class context, compounding audio tokens, and two SKUs. Bake them off. Do not remap them.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Today, 20 September 2026, buyers are still working through Friday's Amazon Bedrock card. [Kimi K3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-moonshot-ai-kimi-k3.html) lists a model launch date of 18 September 2026. The named product is Moonshot AI's flagship, served as `global.moonshotai.kimi-k3` or `us.moonshotai.kimi-k3`. [Inside AI](https://insideai.news/news/ai-in-business/kimi-k3-amazon-bedrock/12298/) dated a recap 19 September. AWS's Builder Center tested Kimi Code 2.0.1 against the Oregon runtime the same day the card went live.

The weights are not new. Moonshot published Kimi K3 in mid-July and put [open weights](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) on Hugging Face on 27 July as `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, under the Kimi K3 License. AWS's 30 July [HyperPod note](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/deploying-kimi-k3-on-amazon-sagemaker-hyperpod-and-amazon-eks/) already described a 2.8 trillion parameter mixture of experts, about 104 billion active per token, 896 experts with 16 routed, a 1,048,576 token context, and native vision. Friday is a managed Bedrock SKU. It is not a new checkpoint and not a silent remap of [Nova Premier](/blog/amazon-nova-premier-eol-bedrock).

Two meters matter on the card. Standard Global cross-Region inference is $3.00 input, $15.00 output, $0.30 cache read, and $3.75 cache write per million tokens, with a 30-minute cache. US Geo is 10 percent higher. Explicit prompt caching is on Responses and Chat Completions, with a 1,024 token minimum per checkpoint. Recaps call Kimi K3 the first open-weight Bedrock model to take those explicit cache controls. Implicit caching is on by default. Score a hosted flagship with a cache meter. Do not score a GPU cluster you already own.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Searchers asking whether Kimi K3 is available on Amazon Bedrock now have a verified split. The July weights were a self-host story. Friday is a model ID inside the same control plane that just retired Premier. Premier was Amazon's 1 million token multimodal teacher. K3 also advertises a 1 million token window and vision. AWS will not migrate dead Premier traffic. A bake-off is allowed. A twin is not.

The price is the other split. Global Standard $3/$15 is in [Fable](/blog/claude-fable-5-1-mythos-trusted-access) and [Astra](/blog/gpt-6-astra-computer-use-flagship) territory, not the [DeepSeek V4.1 Flash](/blog/deepseek-v4-1-flash-pricing-api-benchmarks) off-peak $0.15/$0.60 lane. The lever is cache. A $0.30 cache-read rate is 10 percent of uncached input. That only pays if a repo, policy pack, or knowledge prefix actually hits. Flex is 0.5 times Standard. Priority is 1.75 times. Both tiers, and explicit cache, are limited to Responses and Chat Completions. Converse and Invoke stay on Standard on-demand. AWS also warns Converse can throw `InternalServerException` when prior-turn reasoning blocks are left in the thread.

Open weights do not mean a laptop deploy. Hugging Face lists MXFP4 weights, 93 layers, MoonViT-V2, and the Kimi K3 License. AWS's self-host recipe still wants `ml.p6-b300.48xlarge`, eight Blackwell Ultra GPUs, tensor parallel 8, and `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k3`. [NVIDIA's Hugging Face deal](/blog/nvidia-buys-hugging-face-open-model-hub) did not shrink that bill. Bedrock is the product for teams that refuse that cluster. The [broader pricing reset](/blog/ai-model-pricing-is-changing-what-teams-can-ship) still applies: you pay for a living ID, or you pay in GPUs.

paragraphs: Bedrock application teams feel it first. Point new 1 million token jobs at `global.moonshotai.kimi-k3` unless US residency forces `us.moonshotai.kimi-k3`. AWS recommends Chat Completions on `bedrock-runtime`. Place images before text. The `detail` image parameter is honored only on Chat Completions. Video inputs are not supported on this Bedrock endpoint, even though Moonshot's own API accepts video files. Knowledge bases and intelligent prompt routing are listed as unsupported. Do not paste a Premier agent graph onto K3 and call it a cutover.

Self-host and platform teams sit one layer out. If you already reserved p6-b300 capacity, Friday does not retire that path. It adds a metered alternative that stays inside AWS's boundary, which Inside AI flags as the governance pitch versus downloading weights. Kimi Code CLI can talk to Bedrock's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. That is a terminal workflow. It is not the [OpenAI Agents API](/blog/openai-agents-api-codex-harness). Moonshot-reported benches put K3 near [Fable 5](/blog/claude-fable-5-1-mythos-trusted-access) and GPT-5.6 Sol on several coding and agent sets. Those are vendor numbers from the July card, often with the Kimi Code harness. Rerun your own tasks.

Procurement and compliance sit one layer up. Global is about 10 percent cheaper than US Geo. Flex is the batch discount. Priority is the latency premium. The card lists no EOL date and promises at least 45 days' notice, the opposite of this month's [Premier hard fail](/blog/amazon-nova-premier-eol-bedrock). [Enterprise adoption](/blog/enterprise-ai-adoption-what-is-working) still fails when a model ID is treated as infrastructure. A Chinese-developed open-weight flagship on a US cloud is also a policy question Inside AI raised and AWS has not answered in the recaps. Treat that as a watch item, not a finding.

sections.heading: Facts versus predictions
paragraphs: Fact: the Amazon Bedrock Kimi K3 card lists a launch date of 18 September 2026, context of 1 million tokens, and Active lifecycle with at least 45 days' EOL notice. Fact: the documented inference profiles are `global.moonshotai.kimi-k3` and `us.moonshotai.kimi-k3`. Fact: Standard Global prices are $3.00 input, $15.00 output, $0.30 cache read, and $3.75 cache write per million tokens; US Geo is $3.30, $16.50, $0.33, and $4.125. Fact: Priority is 1.75 times Standard and Flex is 0.5 times Standard on Responses and Chat Completions only. Fact: Hugging Face and AWS describe a 2.8T MoE with about 104B active parameters, 896 experts, and 16 routed per token. Fact: Bedrock does not support video inputs on K3. Fact: Nova Premier reached end of life on 14 September and AWS says it will not remap traffic.

Prediction: most broken Premier graphs will land on Nova 2 Lite or another living Amazon SKU before they land on K3, because $15 output is not a default failover. Prediction: cache-hit rate, not GPQA, will decide whether K3 stays in a production router next to [Gemini 3.8 Flash](/blog/gemini-3-8-flash-agent-workhorse). Prediction: headlines will call Friday a 3T model launch. The checkpoint is from July. Friday is distribution. Do not treat a Bedrock ID as proof you can skip evals, and do not treat open weights as a free cluster.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch whether AWS adds an in-Region-only profile, or whether US Geo and Global remain the only paths. Watch cache-hit rates on 1 million token prefixes once explicit checkpoints are in the client. Watch Converse compatibility in LangChain and Strands after the reasoning-block warning. Watch whether video input ever appears on the Bedrock card, or stays on Moonshot's own API. Watch p6-b300 reservations versus the hosted $3/$15 bill. Watch independent DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench runs that do not use the Kimi Code harness. And watch the Premier replacement question. If a workload has to run on Tuesday, it needs a live model ID and a measured cache, not a rumor that K3 is the new Amazon teacher.

sections.heading: FAQ
paragraphs: What is Kimi K3 Amazon Bedrock? It is Moonshot AI's 2.8 trillion parameter open-weight flagship, served as a managed Amazon Bedrock model as of 18 September 2026. The card lists a 1 million token context, native vision, and inference profiles `global.moonshotai.kimi-k3` and `us.moonshotai.kimi-k3`. The July Hugging Face weights are the same class of model. Friday is hosted inference, not a new training run.

Is Kimi K3 available on Amazon Bedrock? Yes. AWS lists the model launch date as 18 September 2026 and the lifecycle as Active. Access is through US Geo and Global cross-Region inference, not a documented single-Region-only profile. Inside AI recapped general availability on 19 September. AWS's Builder Center tested Kimi Code against Bedrock on 18 September.

How much does Kimi K3 cost on Amazon Bedrock? On the Standard tier, Global cross-Region inference is $3.00 per million input tokens, $15.00 per million output tokens, $0.30 per million cache-read tokens, and $3.75 per million cache-write tokens for a 30-minute cache. US Geo is 10 percent higher. Priority is 1.75 times Standard. Flex is 0.5 times Standard. Those two tiers apply only to Responses and Chat Completions.

Is Kimi K3 a Nova Premier replacement? No. Nova Premier, `amazon.nova-premier-v1:0`, reached end of life on 14 September 2026 and AWS says it will not migrate traffic. Kimi K3 is a Moonshot model with a similar 1 million token window and vision, billed at $3/$15 Global. It is a bake-off candidate. It is not a remap and not an Amazon-native teacher SKU.

What is the difference between global.moonshotai.kimi-k3 and us.moonshotai.kimi-k3? The global profile may route to any supported commercial AWS Region and is about 10 percent cheaper. The US Geo profile keeps processing in US geography for residency requirements. AWS documents both as cross-Region inference. Self-hosting `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on HyperPod or EKS is a third path and still needs reserved p6-b300 capacity.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Today, 20 September 2026, buyers are still working through Friday's AI pacing collusion lawsuit. [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/litigation/openai-anthropic-google-spacexai-hit-with-antitrust-lawsuit) dated the recap 18 September at 11:30 p.m. UTC. The Hill's Finya Swai followed Saturday morning. Mint carried an ANI rewrite that cited Politico. The named product is a civil complaint, Buist v. Anthropic PBC, No. 3:26-cv-10693, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, San Francisco Division. The defendants are Anthropic PBC, OpenAI OpCo LLC, SpaceXAI LLC, and Google LLC.

The claim is Section 1 of the Sherman Act. Four paid subscribers say public endorsements of Dario Amodei's 12 September essay, [We Must Pace the Frontier](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier), amount to an agreement among competitors to slow how fast rival products improve. Bloomberg Law quotes the filing: plaintiffs challenge only what the antitrust laws forbid, an agreement among competitors about how fast their competing products will improve. Congress has granted no exemption for that agreement. Trial Lawyers for Justice is counsel. Nicholas C. Rowley is lead, with Andrew T. Tutt, R. Stanton Jones, and Jakob Z. Norman.

There is no answer, no motion to dismiss date, no class certification, and no defendant comment in the first-day recaps. Score a caption and a theory of overcharge. Do not score a [training freeze](/blog/pace-the-frontier-ai-slowdown) or a finding that anyone broke the law.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Searchers asking whether OpenAI and Anthropic were sued for slowing AI now have a verified split. The [Pace the Frontier](/blog/pace-the-frontier-ai-slowdown) briefing covered the essay and the CEO posts. Friday's docket is the first civil case that treats those posts as the agreement. The Hill says Musk wrote "Dario is right," Altman said he agreed, and Hassabis called the proposal the right path forward. Public praise is easy to quote. A meeting of the minds is what a Section 1 plaintiff still has to prove.

The injury theory is a paid-tier overcharge, not a researcher layoff. Unite.AI's readout of the complaint defines a U.S. market for paid consumer subscriptions to general-purpose frontier assistants: ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Gemini. The four defendants allegedly hold at least 80 percent of that paid stack. ChatGPT Plus is cited at about $20 a month. Buist, Hunt, and Spetsas say they bought all four. Bullock subscribed to Claude. The proposed class is every U.S. person who, from 12 September 2026 through the end of the alleged effects, bought a paid individual subscription directly from a defendant. That is a subscriber case. It is not the [2030 jobs print](/blog/anthropic-ai-jobs-2030-econ-scenarios).

It also tests the safety calendar the labs just advertised. The complaint, as Unite.AI recaps it, does not challenge unilateral safety, independent slowing, lawful research, government compliance, or petitioning Congress. It targets a horizontal deal on rate, compute caps, coordinated release delays, capability checkpoints, or information exchanged to police those limits. That is why buyers should keep the [standards-body talks](/blog/ai-standards-body-anthropic-openai-google) and the [Faculty embed](/blog/anthropic-accenture-embedded-evaluator) on separate lines. A working group is not a cartel finding. A paid desk is not a freeze.

paragraphs: Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Google legal and policy desks feel it first. SpaceXAI is the caption name for the Grok company. The Hill still writes Space XAI in one line. Ask whether Friday's posts are treated as puffery, as parallel independent views, or as an offer and acceptance. Amodei's own essay flagged a narrow antitrust waiver for safety talk. Senator Josh Hawley already said he would not bless three or four firms colluding. The complaint now makes that waiver fight a live exhibit, not a panel talking point.

Paid ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Gemini subscribers sit one layer out. They are the proposed class, not a certified one. The ask is treble damages under the Clayton Act and an injunction against maintaining or monitoring a horizontal pace deal. Plaintiffs say they do not want to ban a lab from slowing on its own. Until a judge certifies anyone, do not treat your $20 receipt as a ticket. IPO and ship buyers should read the same caption next to [OpenAI's listing delay](/blog/openai-ipo-delay-2026-safety) and any [pre-IPO Anthropic SKU](/blog/anthropic-new-model-ipo-astra). A pending Section 1 case is a disclosure item. It is not a blocked [Astra](/blog/gpt-6-astra-computer-use-flagship) date.

Washington and the still-unsigned referee are in the blast radius too. CNBC on 15 September confirmed OpenAI had been talking to Anthropic and Google since the July standards proposal. Chris Lehane said the company would work with or without a government blessing. Plaintiff Cheyenne Hunt, in the ANI recap, called the weekend posts a pinky promise that gave Speaker Mike Johnson cover to adjourn before a binding AI bill. That is her claim. It is not a court finding. [Microsoft's MAI consultation](/blog/microsoft-mai-code-of-conduct-consultation) is still a comment period, not a fourth defendant.

sections.heading: Facts versus predictions
paragraphs: Fact: on 18 September 2026, Charles Buist, Nick Spetsas, Cheyenne Hunt, and Christine Bullock filed Buist v. Anthropic PBC, No. 3:26-cv-10693, in the Northern District of California. Fact: the complaint names Anthropic PBC, OpenAI OpCo LLC, SpaceXAI LLC, and Google LLC and pleads a Section 1 Sherman Act claim, plus Clayton Act damages and an injunction. Fact: Bloomberg Law, The Hill, Mint/ANI citing Politico, and Unite.AI all treat Friday as a filed complaint, not a ruling. Fact: first-day recaps say the companies did not immediately comment. Fact: the filing, as Unite.AI recaps it, does not challenge unilateral safety choices or petitioning government. Fact: no class has been certified and no temporary restraining order has been reported.

Prediction: the first real court paper will be a motion to dismiss arguing that public essays are speech, not a contract. Prediction: labs will keep shipping [Fable](/blog/claude-fable-5-1-mythos-trusted-access), Astra, Gemini, and [Grok](/blog/grok-4-8-release-date) while they brief that motion. Prediction: headlines will keep saying the industry has already agreed to slow down. That is the plaintiffs' sentence. It is not Friday's docket status. Do not treat a complaint as proof of a cartel, and do not treat the absence of a comment as a guilty plea.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch whether any defendant answers or moves to dismiss, and on what theory: no agreement, no output restriction, or no antitrust injury. Watch whether a judge certifies a nationwide paid-subscriber class or trims it to one product. Watch whether the injunction language reaches compute caps and release dates, or dies at the pleading stage. Watch whether Faculty, METR, or a standards-body charter is cited as evidence of coordination or as proof of independent safety work. Watch ship calendars for Astra, Fable, Grok, and Gemini against the 12 September class start. And watch Congress. Hawley already opposed a waiver. A pending case makes that vote harder, not easier.

sections.heading: FAQ
paragraphs: What is the AI pacing collusion lawsuit? It is a proposed class action filed on 18 September 2026 in the Northern District of California as Buist v. Anthropic PBC, No. 3:26-cv-10693. Four paid subscribers accuse Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Google of agreeing to slow how fast rival frontier assistants improve. The claim is Section 1 of the Sherman Act. There is no verdict.

Were OpenAI and Anthropic sued for slowing AI? They were named, with SpaceXAI and Google, in Friday's complaint. The allegation is not that any lab slowed on its own. The allegation is that public endorsements of Amodei's 12 September essay, plus earlier standards talks, add up to a horizontal agreement. Bloomberg Law and The Hill both stress that the companies had not commented in the first recaps.

Is Pace the Frontier illegal collusion? Not on any court's finding. Pace the Frontier is Amodei's essay and a set of public CEO posts. The lawsuit is a plaintiff theory that those posts are an agreement about product improvement speed. Plaintiffs say they do not challenge unilateral safety or petitioning government. A judge has not decided either point.

Who filed Buist v Anthropic? Charles Buist and Nick Spetsas of Florida, and Cheyenne Hunt and Christine Bullock of California, each as individuals and for a proposed nationwide class. Hunt, Buist, and Spetsas say they paid for Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemini. Bullock subscribed to Claude. Nicholas C. Rowley of Trial Lawyers for Justice is lead counsel.

Does the lawsuit freeze ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Gemini? No reported order stops training or a release. Plaintiffs ask for an injunction against a horizontal pace deal and for treble damages. They say a lab may still slow by itself. Until a court certifies a class or issues relief, treat Friday as a docket entry. Do not treat it as a ship-date stay.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Today, 19 September 2026, buyers are still working through Thursday's Anthropic Institute note. [Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs](https://www.anthropic.com/institute/measuring-pace-of-ai-development) landed as Reuters, Bloomberg, the Associated Press, and Business Insider recast it as Claude building the next Claude. The named product is the Anthropic R&D Automation Index, a prototype work basket, not a model card. As of August 2026, Claude "leads" 26% of Anthropic's AI research and development. The share of work at or above "AI collaborates" is above 90%. Claude is not operating fully autonomously for any measured subset.

Lead is a defined term. Anthropic adopted Epoch AI's 0 to 5 automation scale. At AL4, the model completes most of a task end to end from a high-level prompt while a human supervises, course-corrects, and still ships. At AL5, the model notices the work, scopes it, and deploys without a required human. That AL5 line is also Anthropic's public definition of recursive self-improvement: a model fully autonomously building its successor. The August print is 26% AL4 and 0% AL5. Reuters dated the recap 17 September. The Los Angeles Times carried the AP rewrite on Friday.

Two other meters rode along. About 30,000 agents were doing research and engineering on the most-used internal platform at any one time in August. Every action on that platform passes an online monitor before it runs. Of more than a billion decisions that month, about 0.002%, one in 47,000, were blocked. A July 13 to 20 compute snapshot put about 6% of AI R&D compute on safety work, and about 12% of AI-driven AI R&D compute. Both shares are conservative: dual-use tokens counted as capability. Score a first public work-share print. Do not score a researcher layoff or a [training freeze](/blog/pace-the-frontier-ai-slowdown).

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Searchers asking whether Claude now builds the next Anthropic model have a verified split. [Pace the Frontier](/blog/pace-the-frontier-ai-slowdown) named recursive self-improvement as the reason to slow capability gains. Thursday's index is the first lab-owned meter for how much of that loop is already automated. It is not the loop closing. The 26% figure is a person-time-weighted share of a frozen July task tree, 542 nodes, 378 leaves, about 15,000 sampled tasks. It is not 26% of headcount and not 26% of tokens.

The judge is also Claude. Anthropic says staff who own the work areas later rated the same categories without seeing the model evidence. Model-versus-human exact agreement was 59%. Human-versus-human was 35%. Ratings sat within one level 97% of the time. That is a useful check. It is not an independent audit. The [Accenture Faculty embed](/blog/anthropic-accenture-embedded-evaluator) is the desk Anthropic says will later verify metrics like these. Faculty is named. It is not seated on this print.

The job question is narrower than the [2030 economy-wide scenarios](/blog/anthropic-ai-jobs-2030-econ-scenarios). Those paths model US cognitive occupations. This print models the desks that write [Fable, Mythos](/blog/claude-fable-5-1-mythos-trusted-access), and any [pre-IPO SKU](/blog/anthropic-new-model-ipo-astra). AL4 means a researcher still approves the pipeline fix. AL5 would mean the researcher is optional. [Z.AI's Fully Self-Training](/blog/z-ai-5-billion-fully-self-training-glm) filing called recursive self-improvement a technical vision. Anthropic's AL5 line is the same claim with a number attached: zero, for now.

image.caption: AL4 still needs a person to ship. AL5 is the recursive self-improvement line. Do not collapse them into one job-cut headline.

paragraphs: Anthropic research scientists and research engineers feel it first. The company's own Responsible Scaling Policy treats full substitution of that set, at competitive cost, as an AI R&D threshold. Thursday's note does not say the threshold was crossed. It says Claude can take a failure alert, find the broken stage, write and test a fix, and hand back a write-up. The human still decides whether it ships tonight. That is a change in who does the middle of the ticket. It is not a published reduction in researcher seats, unlike [Meta's Project OT cuts](/blog/meta-project-ot-ai-job-cuts).

Buyers and policy desks sit one layer out. A 26% AL4 share with 100% pre-execution monitoring is the oversight claim they can take to a board. A 6% safety-compute share is the resource claim. Anthropic says those figures would be expected to move if labs actually paced the frontier, and that any developer could publish the same three meters. Until OpenAI, Google, or xAI print a comparable basket, this is a single-lab prototype. The [evaluation bottleneck](/blog/ai-research-evaluation-and-safety-bottleneck) did not close because the judge and the worker share a brand.

Agent platform teams should read the 30,000-agent count next to the [OpenAI Agents API](/blog/openai-agents-api-codex-harness), not next to a consumer chat SKU. Coverage is 100% on one internal scaffold. Offline monitors flag about 100,000 transcripts a week and escalate about 50 to humans. That is a review load, not a misalignment rate. The one-in-47,000 block figure is a filter trip, not a count of harmful intent. Do not staff either number into a 2026 hiring plan without the next monthly print.

sections.heading: Facts versus predictions
paragraphs: Fact: Anthropic published the R&D Automation Index on 17 September 2026 and said Claude leads 26% of AI R&D as of August, up from about 1% in March, with more than 90% of work at or above AL3. Fact: no measured subset is AL5. Fact: the index used about 15,000 July tasks, a frozen tree of 542 nodes, and person-time weights; Claude agents catalogued and judged the work. Fact: about 30,000 agents ran on the main internal platform in August, 100% of their actions hit an online monitor, and about 1 in 47,000 of more than a billion decisions were blocked. Fact: in the week of 13 to 20 July, about 6% of AI R&D compute and about 12% of AI-driven AI R&D compute went to safety, on a conservative definition. Fact: Faculty is not named as the verifier of this print.

Prediction: the next monthly index moves the AL4 share before any AL5 cell lights up. Prediction: other labs will praise the idea and decline to publish a matching basket until a referee exists. Prediction: headlines will keep saying Claude is replacing itself. That is the AL5 sentence. It is not the August number. Do not treat 26% as a 26% cut to Anthropic research headcount, and do not treat Thursday as proof that the [2030 extreme jobs path](/blog/anthropic-ai-jobs-2030-econ-scenarios) has started.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the next Anthropic R&D Automation Index print, and whether AL5 is still zero. Watch whether Faculty, METR, or another embed reruns the judge on a subsample the lab did not score. Watch whether OpenAI's unexpected-behavior reports, promised the day before this note, include a comparable work-share number. Watch the 6% safety-compute share across more than one July week. Watch researcher and engineer hiring against the 30,000-agent count. And watch the [roles at risk](/blog/ai-jobs-roles-at-risk-and-roles-being-created) inside labs, not only in the wider cognitive workforce. A lead share is a job design change. It is not yet a layoff memo.

sections.heading: FAQ
paragraphs: What is the Anthropic R&D Automation Index? It is a prototype meter Anthropic published on 17 September 2026. The lab catalogued AI R&D tasks, rated each category on Epoch AI's 0 to 5 automation scale, and weighted the basket by person-time. As of August 2026, Claude leads 26% of that basket at AL4. More than 90% of work is at least AL3. No measured subset is AL5.

Does Claude lead 26% of Anthropic R&D? Yes, on Anthropic's August 2026 print. Lead means AL4: Claude completes most of a task from a high-level prompt while a human supervises and still ships the change. The 26% is a weighted share of a frozen July task tree, not 26% of employees or 26% of compute. The share was about 1% in March.

Is Claude recursively self-improving? Not on Anthropic's own definition. The lab says recursive self-improvement is a model fully autonomously building its successor, which it maps to AL5. Thursday's index says Claude is not fully autonomous on any measured subset of AI R&D. Pace the Frontier still treats the loop as the reason to slow capability gains. The meter and the essay are not the same claim.

What is AL4 vs AL5 in Anthropic's index? AL4, lead, is a human handing Claude a failure alert and reviewing a tested write-up before deploy. AL5, autonomous, is Claude noticing the break, patching it, and shipping without a required human. Anthropic's pipeline footnote makes that split concrete. The August print is 26% AL4 and 0% AL5.

How many AI agents work at Anthropic? About 30,000 research and engineering agents ran at once on the most-used internal platform in August 2026. That count covers one scaffold. Online monitors see 100% of those actions before execution. About 1 in 47,000 of more than a billion August decisions were blocked. Offline monitors flag roughly 100,000 transcripts a week and escalate about 50 to humans.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Today, 19 September 2026, buyers are still working through Friday's Anthropic Accenture notes. Anthropic published [Partnering with Accenture on embedded evaluation](https://www.anthropic.com/news/accenture-embedded-evaluation). Accenture's newsroom posted the same day. CNBC's Ashley Capoot dated the recap 5:31 p.m. Eastern. TechCrunch's Tim Fernholz followed. Reuters and Bloomberg treated it as a $1 billion-each capacity pledge, not a named SKU. Faculty, Accenture's specialist AI unit, will evaluate and red-team models, run alignment assessments, and test safeguards.

The money line is two expectations, not one invoice. Anthropic and Accenture each expect to invest at least $1 billion over five years in building capacity. Anthropic also said that, given urgency, it will fund Accenture's work directly. Long term, the lab still wants pooled or government money, the June Advanced AI Framework ask. Neither pool exists. There is no team size, billing card, start date, or first public report. Score a named embed with employee-comparable access. Do not score a $2 billion purchase order or a [training freeze](/blog/pace-the-frontier-ai-slowdown).

The partnership is non-exclusive. Anthropic says more evaluators will be named in the coming weeks and that it is talking to METR and other nonprofits about pilots that would use their own funding. Accenture says it will do similar work for other AI developers. There are still no standards for what embedded evaluators can see or how they should report. That is the same hole sitting next to the [three-lab standards talks](/blog/ai-standards-body-anthropic-openai-google).

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Searchers asking who Anthropic's first embedded evaluator is now have a verified split. [Pace the Frontier](/blog/pace-the-frontier-ai-slowdown) named METR-class teams with desks, badges, and a right to publish without an editorial veto. Friday's first name is Faculty. Accenture agreed to buy the UK firm on 6 January 2026 and closed on 16 March. Marc Warner, Faculty's CEO, is Accenture's chief technology officer. TechCrunch noted the surprise: the weekend essay pointed at safety nonprofits. The first signed desk is a consultancy that already deploys Claude.

Independence is the product question. In December 2025, Reuters reported Accenture and Anthropic expanding a Claude deal that would train about 30,000 Accenture staff. Faculty had already advised frontier labs on safety before the sale. Anthropic paying Accenture directly is the opposite of the METR lane, where the nonprofit would bring its own funds. TechCrunch said Accenture's shares jumped about 8% after hours. That is a market read on a capacity pledge. It is not a published revenue schedule.

It also tests the IPO and ship calendars. Reuters and CNBC both put this next to Anthropic's listing talk and [GPT-6 Astra](/blog/gpt-6-astra-computer-use-flagship) share. [Anthropic's unnamed pre-IPO model](/blog/anthropic-new-model-ipo-astra) is still a deliberation. An embed that can watch a model take shape in training is the process claim buyers should attach to that SKU. If Faculty cannot publish a finding the lab dislikes, the [evaluation bottleneck](/blog/ai-research-evaluation-and-safety-bottleneck) did not move.

sections.heading: FAQ

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Today, 19 September 2026, HUAWEI CONNECT 2026 closes in Shanghai. Buyers are working through Thursday's keynote from David Wang, Huawei's rotating chairman. He launched the [Huawei Atlas 960E SuperPoD](https://www.huawei.com/en/news/2026/9/hc-ascend960-supernode), which the company calls the industry's first SuperPoD built on near-packaged optics. One pod scales to 4,096 NPUs. Huawei's English note puts that box at 8 EFLOPS at FP8 and 16 EFLOPS at FP4, with a fully liquid-cooled orthogonal design and UnifiedBus memory addressing.

The optics are the product. Huawei's Hi-ONE engine, a mass-produced NPO module with a built-in light source, is rated at 7.2 Tbit/s. The company says 5,500 of those engines replace about 48,000 conventional 800G pluggable modules, cut more than 550 kilowatts, and lift availability to 99.8%. Yang Chaobin, who runs the ICT group, put the rest of the stack on stage the same day: UnifiedBus LinkBlade inside the cabinet, LinkDevice between cabinets, a UBG switch across clusters, an upgraded TaiShan 950 SuperPoD with a 256 TB memory pool, and OceanStor M900 as petabyte-scale KV cache.

Score a systems announcement with named interconnects and a public NPU count. Do not score a die that beats Nvidia's B300, a merchant GPU SKU, or a million-NPU cluster that exists in a hall. TechCrunch's Kate Park dated the chip calendar 17 September: a Huawei spokesperson said the Ascend 960DT is expected in the first quarter of 2027, three quarters earlier than the prior Q3 2027 plan, with the 960PR still in the third quarter. China tech analyst Rui Ma flagged the other number. Last year's Atlas 960 SuperPoD chart said 15,488 Ascend 960 chips. This week's Atlas 960E holds 4,096.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Searchers asking what a Huawei SuperPoD is now have a verified split. The chip moved up. The pod that Huawei put on the 2026 keynote is smaller than the 2025 chart, and the story is wiring, not a process-node miracle. Huawei has said for a year that export controls on advanced lithography pushed it to combine more accelerators instead of waiting for a denser die. That is cousin to the [ASML High NA](/blog/asml-high-na-euv-intel-tsmc-samsung) calendar, not a rebuttal of it. Near-packaged optics sit the optical engine next to the switch chip on the board. They are not co-packaged optics. KR-Asia noted Nvidia and Broadcom already ship CPO switches. Huawei told Nikkei that NPO parts are pluggable, which is a service argument, not a bandwidth trophy.

The software half is the CUDA problem restated. CANN is now community-driven open source. The Next Web said external developers make up 61% of that community, and that Ascend is listed as a PyTorch accelerator backend. That is the same moat [NVIDIA's CUDA-Q](/blog/nvidia-cuda-q-logical-fault-tolerant-quantum) and the [Hugging Face hub deal](/blog/nvidia-buys-hugging-face-open-model-hub) sit on. A SuperPoD without kernels is a dark hall. A SuperPoD with PyTorch and DeepSeek Harness plugins is a domestic training option.

It also tests the pacing debate. TechCrunch noted Xu telling the Financial Times that Chinese firms still need to accelerate before they can judge frontier risk. [Pace the Frontier](/blog/pace-the-frontier-ai-slowdown) is a US-lab pledge. This keynote is a scale-up pledge. Trump and Xi are due in Washington on 24 September. Score a calendar collision, not a treaty.

Prediction: the 4,096-NPU Atlas 960E ships in 2027 before anyone builds the 15,488 chart as a single logical machine. Prediction: per-chip Nvidia gaps stay the talking point outside China, and interconnect utilization stays the talking point inside it. Prediction: export rules, not FLOPS slides, decide whether this kit shows up in Europe. Do not treat 8 EFLOPS as a public bake-off against Blackwell, and do not treat a million NPUs as a purchase order.

sections.heading: What to watch next

sections.heading: FAQ
paragraphs: What is the Huawei Atlas 960E SuperPoD? It is Huawei's NPO-based AI cluster announced at CONNECT 2026 on 17 September. One SuperPoD uses UnifiedBus and Hi-ONE near-packaged optics to treat up to 4,096 NPUs as a single logical machine for training and inference on models Huawei says approach 10 trillion parameters.

How many NPUs does the Atlas 960E SuperPoD have? Huawei's 17 September 2026 English note says 4,096. That is not last year's Atlas 960 chart of 15,488 Ascend 960 chips. TechCrunch quoted analyst Rui Ma on that gap. Ask which SKU is on a 2027 quote.

When will the Huawei Atlas 960E SuperPoD be available? Huawei Central dated commercial availability to the third quarter of 2027. Huawei's English launch note did not print a ship date. The Ascend 960DT chip is separately expected in Q1 2027, according to a Huawei spokesperson speaking to TechCrunch, with the 960PR inference chip still in Q3 2027.

Does the Huawei SuperPoD beat Nvidia? Not on a public per-chip bake-off. The Next Web, citing The Register, still puts the 960DT at roughly half the FP8 and a third of the FP4 compute of Nvidia's B300. Nvidia cannot sell the B300 in China. Huawei's claim is cluster scale, optics, and utilization, not a faster individual accelerator.

What is near-packaged optics in the Atlas 960E? NPO places an optical engine next to the switch chip on the board, short of co-packaged optics that sit inside the same package. Huawei's Hi-ONE module is rated at 7.2 Tbit/s with a built-in light source. The company says 5,500 of them replace about 48,000 800G pluggables and cut more than 550 kilowatts.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Today, 19 September 2026, buyers are still working through Friday's TechCrunch briefing and Thursday night's Wall Street Journal exclusive on Hacktron. Harsh Jaiswal, Mohan Pedhapati, and Rahul Maini used [Claude Opus 5](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-5) to chain two bugs and reach OpenAI staff ChatGPT and Codex accounts. The Journal's Robert McMillan dated the exclusive 17 September. TechCrunch's Aditya Mehta and Rebecca Bellan followed on 18 September. The Hacker News recap landed this morning. OpenAI paid $6,500 on 1 September. The work itself was 25 July.

The path started on community.openai.com, the public help forum that runs on Discourse. A crafted HEIF image hit an old libheif build in the image-conversion path. Discourse's advisory, GHSA-vhm9-85gw-x335, rates that class of upload as remote code execution, CVSS 8.8, tracked as CVE-2026-32882. From the forum, an OpenAI single-sign-on weakness turned control of the box into takeover of ChatGPT and Codex sessions for people who used Sign in with OpenAI. One employee's Codex was connected to OpenAI's GitHub organization. The team prompted that account to open harmless pull request 1186742 in the internal monorepo, then stopped. They say they did not read source, merge, or touch customer data.

Score a disclosed bug bounty with a named trio, a paid SSO finding, and a public Discourse advisory. Do not score a rogue Claude, a production outage, or the [Gemini Irregular](/blog/gemini-hacked-three-companies-irregular) wet-test story. This is human-directed research with a model in the loop. OpenAI said the award recognizes the OpenAI-side finding, not the actions against Discourse, which sat outside the bug bounty program.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Searchers asking whether Claude hacked OpenAI now have a verified split. Claude did not wander out of a sandbox. Three researchers steered it. Opus 4.8, including a cyber-researcher build, stalled once a common memory defense was on. Anthropic shipped Opus 5 on 24 July. Hacktron gave it the same problem and had a working local path within hours, then ported it. TechCrunch quoted Gray Swan CEO Matt Fredrikson: for $200 a month, anyone can use these tools and hack into a company like OpenAI. Pedhapati's line is tighter. AI is reducing the scarce expertise needed to turn a known bug into a working chain. Months became days.

The product lesson is identity, not a new SKU. Hacktron says the escalate step is not Discourse-specific. Any first-party or third-party service on the same OpenAI SSO could have granted the same ChatGPT and Codex access. Forum members who worked at OpenAI did not have to click. That is why this sits next to the [OpenAI Agents API](/blog/openai-agents-api-codex-harness), not on top of [Claude Fable 5.1](/blog/claude-fable-5-1-mythos-trusted-access). Codex with a GitHub connector is a privileged session. A stolen session is a stolen connector. Slack and mail were in the theoretical blast radius and unused.

It also tests the gating story. Mythos 5.1 is the dual-use lane Anthropic locked down over advanced hacking concerns. Opus 5 is the $5 input and $25 output workhorse, generally available, and the model that cleared the hurdle. [Pace the Frontier](/blog/pace-the-frontier-ai-slowdown) is a pledge about capability releases. This write-up is a point release that already shipped. Treat it as neighbor to Anthropic's own [distillation threat report](/blog/anthropic-claude-distillation-threat-report), which already said criminal and state-backed groups use Claude on real intrusions, and as cousin to the [Hugging Face](/blog/nvidia-buys-hugging-face-open-model-hub) agent incident, which was a model acting inside a wet eval. Different actor. Same year of cheap offensive labor.

paragraphs: OpenAI identity and connector owners feel it first. If ChatGPT or Codex shares a login with a public community surface, the questionnaire is simple: which services inherit that session, and which staff GitHub, Slack, or mail links would ride along. Do not wait for a named CVE on the SSO side. OpenAI has not published the identity bug. The 14-hour fix and the $6,500 note are the public record.

Self-hosted Discourse operators sit one layer out. Discourse-hosted customers were patched. Self-hosted sites need the rebuilt image, not a web-interface bump, because the vulnerable libheif lived in the Debian layer. Patched core trains are 2026.7.0, 2026.6.1, 2026.5.2, and 2026.1.6. Debian published DSA-6417-1 for libheif on 8 August. If you still decode untrusted HEIF, HEIC, or AVIF, sandbox the converter or turn the format off. That advice is in Discourse's advisory and in ImageMagick's own security policy. It is not a request to re-run anyone's image file.

Security teams using frontier models as assistants should keep the human in the loop claim honest. Hacktron says this was not fully autonomous hacking. They also say they pointed Opus 5 at their own test forum framed as a capture-the-flag target after the model refused a live remote job. That is a product-control story for [Mythos trusted access](/blog/claude-fable-5-1-mythos-trusted-access) and for [evaluation harnesses](/blog/ai-research-evaluation-and-safety-bottleneck). It is not a how-to. Wider HEIF Heist claims, including Slack, Meta, GitHub Enterprise, and Next.js, are uneven. The Hacker News already flagged that limit. Shopify is the only name Hacktron says noticed the noise.

sections.heading: Facts versus predictions
paragraphs: Fact: the Wall Street Journal reported on 17 September 2026 that researchers used Anthropic's Claude to reach OpenAI, and TechCrunch followed on 18 September. Fact: Hacktron names Jaiswal, Pedhapati, and Maini, dates the chain 25 July, and says it took under 72 hours from first look to the internal pull request. Fact: OpenAI confirmed a fix about 14 hours after the Bugcrowd report and paid $6,500 on 1 September for the OpenAI-side finding. Fact: Discourse published GHSA-vhm9-85gw-x335 on 28 July for CVE-2026-32882 at CVSS 8.8. Fact: Opus 4.8 struggled with a working path once ASLR was on, and Opus 5, shipped 24 July, produced one within hours. Fact: the proof was a single harmless pull request, with no source read and no customer data. Fact: this is not the May Irregular Gemini test.

Prediction: OpenAI will not publish a full SSO post-mortem. Prediction: buyers will add Codex connector reviews before they add a Claude ban. Prediction: the next write-up in this class will name a staff agent connector, not a new model string. Do not treat a $6,500 bounty as proof the next Opus point release will empty a lab, and do not treat three researchers as a nation-state.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch whether OpenAI describes the SSO bug in a security note, or leaves the 14-hour fix as the whole record. Watch whether Codex and ChatGPT connectors get a step-up prompt before GitHub, Slack, or mail actions. Watch whether Anthropic moves any of this pattern into the Mythos gate, or keeps Opus 5 generally available at $5 and $25 per million tokens. Watch Discourse rebuild numbers, not changelog blurbs, on self-hosted fleets. Watch whether HEIF Heist names get independent advisories, or stay a campaign label. And watch the next [Astra](/blog/gpt-6-astra-computer-use-flagship) or Codex session that can click a repo. The interesting failure here was a shared login plus a staff connector, not a model that decided to defect.

sections.heading: FAQ
paragraphs: Did researchers use Claude to hack OpenAI? Yes. Hacktron's three-person team used Claude Opus 5, after Opus 4.8 stalled, to help chain a Discourse image bug and an OpenAI SSO weakness. They reached staff ChatGPT and Codex accounts on 25 July 2026, proved access with a harmless internal pull request, and reported the findings. OpenAI paid $6,500. This was a bug bounty, not a rogue-agent breakout.

What is the Hacktron Claude Opus 5 OpenAI chain? An old libheif build on OpenAI's public Discourse forum accepted a crafted HEIF upload. From that foothold, an OpenAI SSO issue let the researchers take over ChatGPT and Codex sessions of forum users, including staff, with no victim click. One Codex account was linked to OpenAI's GitHub organization. The team opened pull request 1186742 as proof and stopped.

How much did OpenAI pay Hacktron? $6,500, awarded 1 September 2026. OpenAI said the award recognizes the OpenAI-side SSO finding. Testing against the Discourse-hosted community.openai.com forum was explicitly outside the bug bounty program. Discourse patched on 27 July and published its advisory the next day.

Is this the same as Gemini hacking three companies? No. The Gemini story is a May Irregular capture-the-flag test where a wet harness let a model reach three real companies. Hacktron is human-directed security research against OpenAI, using Claude as a tool, disclosed through Bugcrowd. Same season of AI cyber news. Different actor, different bug class, different disclosure path.

Does Claude Opus 5 write exploits now? Hacktron says Opus 5 produced a working path on a problem Opus 4.8 could not finish once ASLR was on, and that skilled humans still directed the work. Anthropic ships Opus 5 as a generally available model at $5 input and $25 output per million tokens. Mythos is the tighter dual-use lane. Treat the write-up as evidence that offensive labor got cheaper, not as a product spec that Opus 5 is an exploit engine.
